headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Claude Code can write/egress broadly while Pipecat can relay content through shared buses and third-party AI services.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads/writes repo files and user directories, and Pipecat commonly moves text through shared bus transports and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible file-to-bus bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be interpreted by the other. The pair is not directly documented as interacting, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Claude Code ingests Pipecat-generated text from a shared file or bus without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Pipecat forwards content from a shared bus into prompts or tool instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer Claude Code.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent message.
Require manual review before Claude Code consumes Pipecat output.
Separate shared files into read-only and write-only paths.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from bus messages.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, while Pipecat can send text/audio/video to multiple third-party STT/LLM/TTS APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or passes transcripts/code between them, sensitive material can leave the host through Pipecat’s outbound services. The profiles support this pathway directly, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Claude Code output containing secrets or code is forwarded into Pipecat services, leakage occurs.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace and Pipecat uploads transcript/context to external APIs, sensitive data can exfiltrate.
mitigations: Do not route secrets into Pipecat services.
Use a redaction step before any handoff.
Restrict Pipecat to local-only models/services.
Separate sensitive repos from Pipecat workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has broad filesystem write, shell, and git mutation; Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency across processes and machines. If both touch the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git state changes can race and corrupt state. Because Claude Code explicitly modifies git state and Pipecat’s shared bus implies multi-instance coordination, the conflict is materially dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git branch, race conditions can corrupt files or history.
IF Pipecat instances share a bus while Claude Code edits the same workspace, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize git writes through one operator.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Lock shared files before edits.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around the shared bus and repo.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, facts, or commands, and Pipecat can consume text in real time and route it into downstream LLM or transport services. If Pipecat treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into spoken responses or automated actions. The pair lacks direct evidence of such a pipeline, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards Claude Code output to a downstream action or response without verification, errors propagate.
IF Claude Code emits incorrect code or facts that Pipecat renders to users, the mistake becomes user-visible.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat acts on Claude Code output.
Require human approval for downstream actions.
Constrain Claude Code output to structured schemas.
Log and diff all handoffs.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, and environment secrets, while Pipecat can process audio, video, images, text, and analytics and may send them to third-party providers. If regulated data such as customer audio or sensitive code is bridged between them, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF regulated audio or text is routed from Claude Code into Pipecat cloud services, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF the same data class is retained by Pipecat analytics longer than the repo workflow expects, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Pipecat cloud services.
Document retention for each handoff.
Use region-locked providers only.
Minimize logged payloads.
requires-engineering: align DPA, residency, and retention controls across the pair.
